column1: # Does normal LoRA management churn the HTTPRoute?
# Asked because istiod 1.30.3 crash-loops under rapid HTTPRoute churn (FINDINGS
# 27), and the obvious conclusion - that adding adapters could storm the control
# plane - turns out to be wrong.
# Measured by sampling svc-a-kserve-route's metadata.resourceVersion every 2s.
# So an adapter change costs exactly one write with no amplification, and the
# route is completely stable at rest. The harness churn was one to two orders of
# magnitude faster and is not a workload anything real produces. The istiod race
# is real and worth reporting upstream, but it is not a LoRA problem and is not an
# argument for or against any route shape.
# The remove case also reconfirms the narrowing of #279: reducing the adapter list
